data.narrative:
Blue Energy, a Growth-stage nuclear energy company founded by Jake Jurewicz, has raised $380M to date. The valuation universe spans 8 comparable companies—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 5 private peers including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Stratek Global—though the narrow peer set at identical stage and valuation tier remains sparse.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach, using the $380M in total capital raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x multiplier typical for Growth-stage companies advancing to later funding rounds. This yields $456M. Peer-median analysis was not applied; while 4 same-sector comparables exist, insufficient overlap across stage, timing, and valuation tier (fewer than 3 datapoints meeting narrow criteria) rendered sector-wide medians potentially misleading and inapplicable.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $388M (low) to $524M (high), with a median of $456M. This range is derived from a single quantitative method, introducing material dependence on stage-progression assumptions. Key uncertainties include Blue Energy's specific technology maturity, capital efficiency relative to peers, regulatory pathway clarity, and commercial timeline—variables not captured in capital-raise proxies. A peer-median approach would strengthen conviction once comparable companies reach similar developmental milestones or sufficient narrow-set datapoints emerge.
